summary: A UNEP web page introducing sustainable lifestyles as ways of living and social choices that minimize environmental degradation while supporting equitable development and quality of life. It argues that a growing global population and resource pressures make lifestyle choices a planetary risk, and that sustainable living first appears in the SDGs (goals 4 and 12.8). The page lists UNEP research reports, tools and resources, and contact details for the Economy Division's Resources and Markets Branch in Paris, with surrounding navigation boilerplate omitted.
one_line: UNEP overview of sustainable lifestyles, linking consumption choices to environmental impact, with related research reports and tools.
key_facts: Sustainable Lifestyles are considered as ways of living, social behaviors and choices, that minimize environmental degradation (use of natural resources, CO2 emissions, waste and pollution) while supporting equitable socio-economic development and better quality of life for all.
By 2050, the world's population may reach a whopping 10 billion.
Two to three billion new urban consumers and youth will receive the majority of their information from social media.
Sustainable living and lifestyles for the first time appear in the Sustainable Development Goals (4 Education and 12.8 Responsible Consumption).
To combat the climate crisis and secure a safe future below 1.5°C, the world needs to cut emissions of planet-warming greenhouse gasses by 50 per cent within the decade.
The policy brief 'Enabling Sustainable Lifestyles in a Climate Emergency' introduces the policy tool of choice-editing.
'1.5-Degree Lifestyles: Towards a Fair Consumption Space for All' analyses lifestyle carbon footprints of ten sample countries, representing high-, middle-, and low-income countries.
The Covid-19 desktop research 'Sustainable Living and Lifestyles: Covid-19 impacts' examines how 'COVID lifestyles' affect the environment.
'Lifestyle Impact on Biodiversity and Nature' aims to identify lifestyle areas with the greatest impacts on biodiversity loss.
'Society and Lifestyles in 2050: Insights from a Global Survey of Experts' projects how disruptions in environment, health, politics and technology will affect lifestyles in 2050.
'1.5-Degree Lifestyles: Targets and options for reducing lifestyle carbon footprints' establishes global targets for lifestyle carbon footprints based on a literature review.
UNEP's Economy Division, Resources and Markets Branch, is located at 1 Rue Miollis, Building VII, 75015 Paris, France.
The page lists tools including The Good Life Goals, The Good Life Goals Business Guide, and The Sustainable Lifestyles Academy.
The page states the aim to 'Empower people to live better and lighter.'
